claims.text: The identity of X governs protective oxide formation and persistence in CrFeCoNiX alloys.
X controls oxidation behavior through oxide-forming-element diffusion kinetics and oxide-phase thermodynamic stability.
CrFeCoNiSi forms a silica scale during high-temperature oxidation.
CrFeCoNiAl forms an alumina scale during high-temperature oxidation.
The silica and alumina scales are coherent, adherent, and slow-growing.
Silica and alumina have low oxygen permeability and therefore limit further oxidation.
Si and Al have lower diffusivity than Mn in the relevant CrFeCoNiX alloys and exposure regime.
SiO2 and Al2O3 are sufficiently thermodynamically stable under the stated conditions to produce persistent protective scales.
Favorable lattice matching between silica or alumina and the alloy matrix causes good scale adhesion.
The manganese-oxide scales are porous and non-coherent.
The manganese-oxide scales crack or spall because of poor lattice matching and higher Mn mobility.
Scale–matrix interfacial integrity and lattice matching mediate whether the oxide is protective.
Under identical exposures, the Si- and Al-containing alloys will exhibit more stable and protective scales than the Mn-containing alloy.
The Mn-containing alloy is expected to provide a non-protective baseline under the stated exposure conditions.
Consistent processing can produce homogeneous, single-phase CrFeCoNiX solid solutions for all three choices of X.
Secondary-phase evolution or other multicomponent interactions could alter oxide-layer formation.

contradictions.description: The conditions and falsification design include exposure at exactly 900 °C ('900 °C and above' and '≥900 °C'), whereas the boundary states that the hypothesis applies only above 900 °C.
